claim: ZIKV M forms oligomeric membrane-permeabilising channels in vitro.
source: Here, we show that M forms oligomeric membrane-permeabilising channels in vitro, with increased activity at acidic pH and sensitivity to the prototypic channel-blocker, rimantadine.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding, which is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript including liposome dye release assays and electron microscopy.

claim: ZIKV M channel activity increases at acidic pH.
source: Here, we show that M forms oligomeric membrane-permeabilising channels in vitro, with increased activity at acidic pH and sensitivity to the prototypic channel-blocker, rimantadine.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B demonstrating pH-dependent dye release.

claim: ZIKV M channel activity is sensitive to rimantadine.
source: Here, we show that M forms oligomeric membrane-permeabilising channels in vitro, with increased activity at acidic pH and sensitivity to the prototypic channel-blocker, rimantadine.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C demonstrating rimantadine inhibition of M channel activity.

claim: Rimantadine blocks an early stage of ZIKV cell culture infection.
source: Accordingly, rimantadine blocked an early stage of ZIKV cell culture infection.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D demonstrating that rimantadine is most effective when added during infection.

claim: Structure-based M channel models comprise hexameric arrangements of two trans-membrane domain protomers.
source: Structure-based channel models, comprising hexameric arrangements of two trans-membrane domain protomers were shown to comprise more stable assemblages than other oligomers using molecular dynamics simulations.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by molecular dynamics simulations presented in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: Hexameric M channel models are more stable than other oligomers based on molecular dynamics simulations.
source: Structure-based channel models, comprising hexameric arrangements of two trans-membrane domain protomers were shown to comprise more stable assemblages than other oligomers using molecular dynamics simulations.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by molecular dynamics simulations comparing different oligomeric states presented in Figure 5 and the Appendix.

claim: M channel models contain a predicted lumenal rimantadine-binding site.
source: Models contained a predicted lumenal rimantadine-binding site, as well as a second druggable target region on the membrane-exposed periphery.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by in silico docking studies shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: M channel models contain a second druggable target region on the membrane-exposed periphery.
source: Models contained a predicted lumenal rimantadine-binding site, as well as a second druggable target region on the membrane-exposed periphery.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by in silico docking studies shown in Figure 6A and experimental validation with compounds targeting this site.

claim: In silico screening enriched for repurposed drugs/compounds predicted to bind to M channel binding sites.
source: In silico screening enriched for repurposed drugs/compounds predicted to bind to either one site or the other.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by the screening results presented in Tables 1 and 2 and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Compounds identified by in silico screening displayed superior potency in vitro compared with rimantadine.
source: Hits displayed superior potency in vitro and in cell culture compared with rimantadine, with efficacy demonstrably linked to virion-resident channels.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B, E, F, and G demonstrating improved EC50 values for compounds like GNF 5837.

claim: Compounds identified by in silico screening displayed superior potency in cell culture compared with rimantadine.
source: Hits displayed superior potency in vitro and in cell culture compared with rimantadine, with efficacy demonstrably linked to virion-resident channels.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B and E demonstrating antiviral effects at lower concentrations than rimantadine.

claim: The efficacy of compounds identified by in silico screening is demonstrably linked to virion-resident channels.
source: Hits displayed superior potency in vitro and in cell culture compared with rimantadine, with efficacy demonstrably linked to virion-resident channels.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7 demonstrating that compounds reduce specific infectivity of purified virions.

claim: Rimantadine effectively blocked ZIKV viraemia in preclinical models.
source: Finally, rimantadine effectively blocked ZIKV viraemia in preclinical models, supporting that M constitutes a physiologically relevant target.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8C demonstrating reduced viraemia in rimantadine-treated mice.

claim: M constitutes a physiologically relevant target for ZIKV antivirals.
source: Finally, rimantadine effectively blocked ZIKV viraemia in preclinical models, supporting that M constitutes a physiologically relevant target.
evidence: The abstract states this conclusion, which is supported by the in vivo efficacy data shown in Figure 8.

claim: ZIKV was first isolated in the Zika forest in Uganda in 1947.
source: Zika virus (ZIKV) was first isolated in the eponymous Ugandan forest in 1947 and is a mosquito-borne arbovirus (arthropod-borne), classified within the Flavivirus genus of the Flaviviridae (Dick, 1952; Dick et al., 1952).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Dick, 1952 and Dick et al., 1952.

claim: ZIKV is a mosquito-borne arbovirus.
source: Zika virus (ZIKV) was first isolated in the eponymous Ugandan forest in 1947 and is a mosquito-borne arbovirus (arthropod-borne), classified within the Flavivirus genus of the Flaviviridae (Dick, 1952; Dick et al., 1952).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Dick, 1952 and Dick et al., 1952.

claim: ZIKV is classified within the Flavivirus genus of the Flaviviridae.
source: Zika virus (ZIKV) was first isolated in the eponymous Ugandan forest in 1947 and is a mosquito-borne arbovirus (arthropod-borne), classified within the Flavivirus genus of the Flaviviridae (Dick, 1952; Dick et al., 1952).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Dick, 1952 and Dick et al., 1952.

claim: Historically, ZIKV caused infrequent and relatively mild infections in humans with symptoms comprising fever, rash, headaches, joint/muscle pain, and conjunctivitis.
source: Historically, ZIKV caused infrequent and relatively mild infections in humans with symptoms comprising fever, rash, headaches, joint/muscle pain, and conjunctivitis (Simpson, 1964).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Simpson, 1964.

claim: A large ZIKV outbreak occurred in 2007 on Yap Island (Micronesia).
source: However, once confined to Africa and Southeast Asia, a large outbreak in 2007 on Yap Island (Micronesia), followed by further outbreaks in French Polynesia, New Caledonia, and the Cook Islands in 2013/14, signified spread of the virus across the Pacific.
evidence: This statement is presented as a historical fact in the introduction.

claim: ZIKV outbreaks occurred in French Polynesia, New Caledonia, and the Cook Islands in 2013/14.
source: However, once confined to Africa and Southeast Asia, a large outbreak in 2007 on Yap Island (Micronesia), followed by further outbreaks in French Polynesia, New Caledonia, and the Cook Islands in 2013/14, signified spread of the virus across the Pacific.
evidence: This statement is presented as a historical fact in the introduction.

claim: ZIKV arrived in Brazil in 2015, where an epidemic affecting >1 M people ensued.
source: The virus then arrived in Brazil in 2015, where an epidemic affecting >1 M people ensued.
evidence: This statement is presented as a historical fact in the introduction.

claim: The ZIKV epidemic in Brazil resulted in worldwide spread of the virus involving more than 80 countries.
source: This resulted in worldwide spread of the virus involving more than 80 countries and signified emergent ZIKV as a global health concern (Lazear and Diamond, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Lazear and Diamond, 2016.

claim: ZIKV outbreaks in Yap and thereafter encompassed more serious symptomology, which has been linked to evolution of New World ZIKV strains.
source: Worryingly, the outbreaks in Yap and thereafter encompassed considerably more serious symptomology, which has been linked to evolution of New World ZIKV strains (Gong et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Gong et al., 2017.

claim: Recent ZIKV outbreaks included more serious and frequent neurological complications.
source: This included more serious and frequent neurological complications, increased incidence of Guillian–Barre syndrome, and a devastating epidemic of microcephaly in new-borns where maternal infection had occurred during the first trimester of pregnancy (Rasmussen and Jamieson, 2020; Rasmussen et al., 2016; Rasmussen et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Rasmussen and Jamieson, 2020; Rasmussen et al., 2016; Rasmussen et al., 2017.

claim: Recent ZIKV outbreaks included increased incidence of Guillian–Barre syndrome.
source: This included more serious and frequent neurological complications, increased incidence of Guillian–Barre syndrome, and a devastating epidemic of microcephaly in new-borns where maternal infection had occurred during the first trimester of pregnancy (Rasmussen and Jamieson, 2020; Rasmussen et al., 2016; Rasmussen et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Rasmussen and Jamieson, 2020; Rasmussen et al., 2016; Rasmussen et al., 2017.

claim: Recent ZIKV outbreaks included a devastating epidemic of microcephaly in new-borns where maternal infection had occurred during the first trimester of pregnancy.
source: This included more serious and frequent neurological complications, increased incidence of Guillian–Barre syndrome, and a devastating epidemic of microcephaly in new-borns where maternal infection had occurred during the first trimester of pregnancy (Rasmussen and Jamieson, 2020; Rasmussen et al., 2016; Rasmussen et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Rasmussen and Jamieson, 2020; Rasmussen et al., 2016; Rasmussen et al., 2017.

claim: The ZIKV outbreak was contained by surveillance combined with control of insect vectors, predominantly Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitos.
source: Eventually, the outbreak was contained by surveillance combined with control of insect vectors, predominantly Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitos (Peterson et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Peterson et al., 2016.

claim: A ZIKV vaccine remains elusive, although several are in trials.
source: More than 7 years later, a ZIKV vaccine remains elusive, although several are in trials (reviewed in Poland et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Poland et al., 2018.

claim: No licensed antiviral therapies exist to treat ZIKV infection.
source: Similarly, no licensed antiviral therapies exist to treat ZIKV infection, yet repurposing of nucleotide analogue inhibitors against the NS5 protein shows promise (Mumtaz et al., 2017; Masmejan et al., 2018; Lim et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Mumtaz et al., 2017; Masmejan et al., 2018; Lim et al., 2020.

claim: Repurposing of nucleotide analogue inhibitors against the NS5 protein shows promise for treating ZIKV infection.
source: Similarly, no licensed antiviral therapies exist to treat ZIKV infection, yet repurposing of nucleotide analogue inhibitors against the NS5 protein shows promise (Mumtaz et al., 2017; Masmejan et al., 2018; Lim et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Mumtaz et al., 2017; Masmejan et al., 2018; Lim et al., 2020.

claim: ZIKV possesses a positive sense single-stranded RNA genome over 10 kb in length.
source: ZIKV, like other Flaviviruses, possesses a positive sense single-stranded RNA genome over 10 kb in length, capped at the 5ʹ end by a methylated dinucleotide (m7GpppAmp) (Garcia-Blanco et al., 2016; Ray et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Garcia-Blanco et al., 2016; Ray et al., 2006.

claim: The ZIKV RNA genome is capped at the 5ʹ end by a methylated dinucleotide (m7GpppAmp).
source: ZIKV, like other Flaviviruses, possesses a positive sense single-stranded RNA genome over 10 kb in length, capped at the 5ʹ end by a methylated dinucleotide (m7GpppAmp) (Garcia-Blanco et al., 2016; Ray et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Garcia-Blanco et al., 2016; Ray et al., 2006.

claim: The ZIKV RNA is translated into a polyprotein that is subsequently cleaved by host and viral proteases to yield 10 mature gene products.
source: The RNA is translated into a polyprotein that is subsequently cleaved by host and viral proteases to yield 10 mature gene products (Assenberg et al., 2009); these are spatially organised into structural virion components at the N-terminus, and non-structural replicase proteins at the C-terminus.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Assenberg et al., 2009.

claim: ZIKV gene products are spatially organised into structural virion components at the N-terminus, and non-structural replicase proteins at the C-terminus.
source: The RNA is translated into a polyprotein that is subsequently cleaved by host and viral proteases to yield 10 mature gene products (Assenberg et al., 2009); these are spatially organised into structural virion components at the N-terminus, and non-structural replicase proteins at the C-terminus.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Assenberg et al., 2009.

claim: The mature ZIKV enveloped virion comprises the viral RNA, the capsid (C) protein and two membrane proteins: envelope (E) and the small membrane (M) protein.
source: The mature enveloped virion comprises the viral RNA, the capsid (C) protein and two membrane proteins: envelope (E) and the small membrane (M) protein (Prasad et al., 2017; Tan et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Prasad et al., 2017; Tan et al., 2020.

claim: ZIKV virions undergo maturation as they traffic through the cell during egress.
source: Virions undergo maturation as they traffic through the cell during egress, with M and the precursor (pr) peptide acting as chaperones for the E protein (Yu et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Yu et al., 2008.

claim: M and the precursor (pr) peptide act as chaperones for the E protein during ZIKV virion maturation.
source: Virions undergo maturation as they traffic through the cell during egress, with M and the precursor (pr) peptide acting as chaperones for the E protein (Yu et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Yu et al., 2008.

claim: ZIKV maturation occurs upon furin-mediated cleavage of pr-M in the Golgi.
source: Maturation occurs upon furin-mediated cleavage of pr-M in the Golgi (Stadler et al., 1997; Sevvana et al., 2018), although this has variable efficiency (Dowd et al., 2014; Junjhon et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Stadler et al., 1997; Sevvana et al., 2018.

claim: Furin-mediated cleavage of pr-M has variable efficiency.
source: Maturation occurs upon furin-mediated cleavage of pr-M in the Golgi (Stadler et al., 1997; Sevvana et al., 2018), although this has variable efficiency (Dowd et al., 2014; Junjhon et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Dowd et al., 2014; Junjhon et al., 2008.

claim: The cleaved pr peptide remains associated with E, preventing exposure of the fusion loop within acidifying secretory vesicles.
source: The cleaved pr peptide remains associated with E, preventing exposure of the fusion loop within acidifying secretory vesicles.
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge about Flavivirus biology.

claim: Release of ZIKV from the cell into a pH-neutral environment leads to the loss of pr and resultant structural rearrangement of E and M.
source: Release from the cell into a pH-neutral environment leads to the loss of pr and resultant structural rearrangement of E and M (Yu et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Yu et al., 2009.

claim: E comprises the essential virus attachment and entry protein.
source: Whilst E comprises the essential virus attachment and entry protein, the role of M within the mature infectious virion remains unknown (Sirohi et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Sirohi et al., 2016.

claim: The role of M within the mature infectious virion remains unknown.
source: Whilst E comprises the essential virus attachment and entry protein, the role of M within the mature infectious virion remains unknown (Sirohi et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Sirohi et al., 2016.

claim: Dimeric M is bound to E dimers within the ZIKV virion.
source: The presence of dimeric M, bound to E dimers (Sirohi et al., 2016), within the virion raises the question of whether it might play a role during the virus entry process.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Sirohi et al., 2016.

claim: Cryo-EM structures of acidified Flavivirus particles do not contain density attributable to the M protein.
source: Unfortunately, cryo-EM structures of acidified Flavivirus particles – a proxy for changes likely to occur during endocytosis – do not contain density attributable to the M protein (Zhang et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2015.

claim: E undergoes a shift from a dimeric to a trimeric form thought to mediate membrane fusion.
source: Moreover, E undergoes a shift from a dimeric to a trimeric form thought to mediate membrane fusion (Bressanelli et al., 2004; Stiasny et al., 2004; Modis et al., 2005; Nayak et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Bressanelli et al., 2004; Stiasny et al., 2004; Modis et al., 2005; Nayak et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2004.

claim: The shift of E from dimeric to trimeric form presumably disrupts E–M dimeric interactions.
source: Moreover, E undergoes a shift from a dimeric to a trimeric form thought to mediate membrane fusion (Bressanelli et al., 2004; Stiasny et al., 2004; Modis et al., 2005; Nayak et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2004). This presumably disrupts E–M dimeric interactions, thereby allowing M an opportunity to also adopt alternative conformations and explore other oligomeric states.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural changes of E protein during fusion.

claim: Dengue virus (DENV) M peptides formed membrane channels in vitro.
source: Interestingly, dengue virus (DENV) M peptides formed membrane channels in vitro (Premkumar et al., 2005), which would require the formation of higher-order oligomers.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Premkumar et al., 2005.

claim: Electrophysiology studies in Xenopus oocytes failed to detect M-mediated proton conductance.
source: However, electrophysiology studies in Xenopus oocytes failed to detect M-mediated proton conductance (Wong et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Wong et al., 2011.

claim: M has long been speculated to comprise a virus-encoded ion channel, or 'viroporin'.
source: Nevertheless, due to its size and hydrophobicity, M has long been speculated to comprise a virus-encoded ion channel, or 'viroporin', typified by the M2 proton channel of influenza A virus (IAV) (Nieva et al., 2012; Royle et al., 2015; Scott and Griffin, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Nieva et al., 2012; Royle et al., 2015; Scott and Griffin, 2015.

claim: IAV M2 functions to allow protons to pass into the virion core during virus entry, enabling the uncoating of viral RNA.
source: M2 functions to allow protons to pass into the virion core during virus entry, enabling the uncoating of viral RNA, and is the target of the antiviral drugs amantadine and rimantadine, setting clinical precedent for viroporins as drug targets.
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge about IAV M2.

claim: IAV M2 is the target of the antiviral drugs amantadine and rimantadine.
source: M2 functions to allow protons to pass into the virion core during virus entry, enabling the uncoating of viral RNA, and is the target of the antiviral drugs amantadine and rimantadine, setting clinical precedent for viroporins as drug targets.
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge about IAV M2.

claim: M peptides form channel-like oligomeric complexes within membrane-mimetic environments.
source: ZIKV M peptides form channel-like oligomeric complexes within membrane-mimetic environments
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 1B and C, and native PAGE data in Figure 1D.

claim: M peptides exhibit dose-dependent dye release using sub-micromolar concentrations.
source: Dose-dependent dye release occurred using sub-micromolar concentrations of M peptide, consistent with channel forming activity (Figure 2A); 780 nM was chosen as an optimal concentration for ensuing investigations.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Mildly acidic pH conditions increased M-mediated release of carboxyfluorescein.
source: Interestingly, mildly acidic pH conditions increased M-mediated release of carboxyfluorescein (CF), reminiscent of IAV M2 (Scott et al., 2020), hepatitis C virus (HCV) p7 (StGelais et al., 2009; Atkins et al., 2014), and human papillomavirus type 16 (HPV16) E5 (Wetherill et al., 2012) in similar experiments (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and citations to similar findings for other viroporins.

claim: Acidic pH conditions mimic those found within endocytic vesicles.
source: Such conditions mimic those found within endocytic vesicles, consistent with M channels potentially being activated during virus entry.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about endocytic vesicle pH.

claim: Rimantadine (1 μM) caused a significant reduction in M channel activity.
source: One such prototype, rimantadine (1 μM), caused a significant reduction in M channel activity (Figure 2C), consistent with the presence of a viable binding site within a soluble, folded M channel complex.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: M peptides form channels within membranes exhibiting significant curvature, such as that seen within an enveloped virion.
source: Finally, we tested whether M peptides were able to form channels within membranes exhibiting significant curvature, such as that seen within an enveloped virion. Liposomes extruded using a 0.05-μM filter provided a similar level of M-induced dye release, albeit with a slightly reduced kinetic, likely due to the increased molar ratio of resulting liposomes to peptide (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Rimantadine exerted a dose-dependent reduction in ZIKV infection of Vero cells.
source: Rimantadine exerted a dose-dependent reduction in ZIKV infection, assessed by both the number of cells infected and ensuing viral protein production (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A-C.

claim: Infected cell numbers underwent statistically significant reductions at rimantadine concentrations of 10 μM and above.
source: Infected cell numbers underwent statistically significant reductions at rimantadine concentrations of 10 μM and above.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Rimantadine affected neither cell viability, nor the uptake of fluorescently labelled EGF over the concentration range tested.
source: Importantly, rimantadine affected neither cell viability, nor the uptake of fluorescently labelled (Epidermal Growth Factor) EGF as a proxy marker for clathrin-mediated endocytosis over the concentration range tested (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Statistically significant reductions of ZIKV infectivity occurred when rimantadine was present during infection.
source: Statistically significant reductions of infectivity occurred when rimantadine was present during infection, with more pronounced effects upon pre-incubating cells with the drug (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Rimantadine affected an early stage of the ZIKV life cycle, coincident with virus entry.
source: Taken together, rimantadine affected an early stage of the virus life cycle, coincident with virus entry.
evidence: This is an inference based on the timing experiments shown in Figure 3D.

claim: M is highly conserved between ZIKV isolates.
source: M is highly conserved between ZIKV isolates (Figure 4A), and regions including the linker region between the first and second alpha helices are shared with other Flaviviruses (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by sequence analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Regions including the linker region between the first and second alpha helices of M are shared with other Flaviviruses.
source: M is highly conserved between ZIKV isolates (Figure 4A), and regions including the linker region between the first and second alpha helices are shared with other Flaviviruses (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by sequence analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Four different TMD prediction software packages revealed disparate outputs for the region known to form the second and third helices within cryo-EM reconstructions.
source: However, four different TMD prediction software packages revealed disparate outputs for the region known to form the second and third helices within cryo-EM reconstructions, with two favouring the formation of an extended single TMD (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by the prediction results shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: MEMSAT-SVM predicted a double TMD topology for M and that helix 3 displayed properties consistent with being pore lining.
source: Interestingly, the MEMSAT-SVM package not only predicted a double TMD topology, but also that helix 3 displayed properties consistent with being pore lining (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by the prediction results shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The cryo-EM-derived conformer of M remained stable for the duration of the simulation.
source: By comparison, the cryo-­EM-­derived conformer structure was simulated in a model bilayer as for C. This conformation remained stable for the duration of the simulation (five repeat simulations, standard deviations in grey).
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The straightened, single TM M protomer exhibited a high degree of movement and flexibility during simulations.
source: Straightened, single TM M protomer inserted into a POPC bilayer and subjected to coarse-grained (CG) simulations for 3 μs, running from start (top) to finished (bottom) pose. (root mean square deviation) RMSD over time (five repeat simulations, standard deviations in grey) showed a high degree of movement and flexibility exhibited by this conformation (~1nm throughout), as the protein appears to attempt moving the C-terminal helix (H3) back along the plain of the membrane.
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The single helix form of M rapidly began to fold back towards the membrane, with helix 3 partially overlaying the phosphate groups of one monolayer.
source: In contrast, the single helix form rapidly began to fold back towards the membrane, with helix 3 partially overlaying the phosphate groups of one monolayer. Hence, this form of the peptide was clearly unstable compared to the cryo-EM structure and we considered it likely that potential higher-order M oligomers also comprised double-TMD protomers.
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Compact hexameric models for M channel complexes comprised of dual-spanning protomers displayed consistent channel-like characteristics compared to an array of alternative conformations and oligomeric states.
source: Compact hexameric models for M channel complexes comprised of dual-spanning protomers displayed consistent channel-like characteristics compared to an array of alternative conformations and oligomeric states, with helix 1 contributing significantly to overall channel stability.
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Helix 1 contributes significantly to overall M channel stability.
source: Compact hexameric models for M channel complexes comprised of dual-spanning protomers displayed consistent channel-like characteristics compared to an array of alternative conformations and oligomeric states, with helix 1 contributing significantly to overall channel stability.
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C demonstrating that removal of helix 1 caused rapid dissociation of the channel complex.

claim: Removal of helix 1 caused the collapse of stable pores within 50 ns in each of three simulations.
source: Accordingly, removal of helix 1 caused the collapse of stable pores within 50 ns in each of three simulations (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), demonstrating its likely importance in the formation of a stable channel complex.
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Compact M hexamer models lined by helix 3 displayed spontaneous closure, consistent with a reasonable physiological representation of a membrane channel.
source: Thus, despite the starting position of this model possessing a relatively wide lumen compared with the diameter of a water column (~1.15 Å), compact M hexamer models lined by helix 3 displayed spontaneous closure, consistent with a reasonable physiological representation of a membrane channel.
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 5C-E.

claim: Channel closing first occurred at 70, 80, and 176 ns within three separate simulations of compact M hexamers.
source: Channel closing first occurred at 70, 80, and 176 ns within three separate simulations, with channels remaining closed for the remainder of the simulation (Figure 5C, D).
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: Mimicking acidic external pH by protonation of His28 had little appreciable effect upon channel opening during simulations.
source: Interestingly, despite the effect of acidic external pH upon M channel activity in vitro (Figure 2B), mimicking such an environment by protonation of a potential candidate pH sensor, His28 within helix 1, had little appreciable effect upon channel opening during simulations.
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 4.

claim: His28Ala mutant peptides responded to acid pH identically to wild-type in vitro.
source: This was confirmed by His28Ala mutant peptides responding to acid pH identically to wild-type in vitro (Figure 5—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 4C.

claim: Other ionisable residues within the M protein likely mediate acid-enhanced activity in vitro.
source: Thus, other ionisable residues within the M protein likely mediate acid-enhanced activity in vitro.
evidence: This is an inference based on the His28 mutation data showing no effect on pH sensitivity.

claim: Docking of rimantadine into the compact M hexamer model revealed an energetically favourable interaction with a lumenal binding site, close in proximity to the region in which channel closure occurred during simulations, termed 'L1'.
source: Docking of rimantadine into the compact M hexamer model revealed an energetically favourable interaction with a lumenal binding site, close in proximity to the region in which channel closure occurred during simulations, termed 'L1' (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by in silico docking data shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The adamantyl cage of rimantadine made predicted hydrophobic contacts with Val61, Ile62, Leu64, Val65, and Leu68.
source: The adamantyl cage of rimantadine made predicted hydrophobic contacts with Val61, Ile62, Leu64, Val65, and Leu68, leaving the methyl group and amine solvent exposed, projecting into the channel lumen (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by in silico docking data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The L1 site underwent predicted interactions with other adamantyl-containing molecules, including amantadine.
source: The same site also underwent predicted interactions with other adamantyl-containing molecules, including amantadine, which adopted a similar predicted binding mode to rimantadine (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by in silico docking data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The lumenal rimantadine site (L1) was the most favourable in terms of druggability score for the compact hexamer model, assessed using the SiteMap programme.
source: Reassuringly, the lumenal rimantadine site (L1) was the most favourable in terms of druggability score for the compact hexamer model, assessed using the SiteMap programme (Maestro, Schrödinger).
evidence: This is supported by computational analysis using SiteMap.

claim: Two other potential lumenal sites were identified with lower predicted druggability scores (L2, L3).
source: Two other potential lumenal sites were also identified with lower predicted druggability scores (L2, L3, Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by computational analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: An additional region upon the membrane-exposed periphery (P1) could undergo interactions with small molecules.
source: However, inspection of the M channel model identified an additional region upon the membrane-exposed periphery that could also undergo interactions with small molecules (P1, Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Two of seven HCV p7-targeted compounds displayed inhibitory effects versus M in dye release assays.
source: Encouragingly, two of the seven compounds tested displayed inhibitory effects versus M in dye release assays, with JK3/42 being most active (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Adamantane derivatives with additional R groups were ineffective at targeting M activity.
source: Interestingly, adamantane derivatives with additional R groups were ineffective at targeting M activity (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), potentially due to the limited size of the L1 cavity.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Twenty-four hits were identified from the L1-targeted short list in dye release assay screens.
source: Dye release assay screens (96-well format) were conducted using compounds at a concentration of one micromolar, with positive hits defined as compounds exerting a 50 ± 5% decrease in M activity (Figure 6—figure supplement 2). Twenty-four hits were identified from the L1-targeted short list, and 15 for the P1 site.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Fifteen hits were identified from the P1-targeted short list in dye release assay screens.
source: Dye release assay screens (96-well format) were conducted using compounds at a concentration of one micromolar, with positive hits defined as compounds exerting a 50 ± 5% decrease in M activity (Figure 6—figure supplement 2). Twenty-four hits were identified from the L1-targeted short list, and 15 for the P1 site.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Each of the six selected compounds exerted a statistically significant reduction upon ZIKV infectivity.
source: Testing at these concentrations revealed that each of the compounds exerted a statistically significant reduction upon ZIKV infectivity, with the most effective showing sub-micromolar potency (Figure 6B), whereas the inactive JK3/32 compound showed no detectable antiviral effects.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: KB SRC 4 displayed antiviral efficacy at 250 nM.
source: Two L1-selected compounds, KB SRC 4 and GNF 5837 displayed antiviral efficacy at 250 and 80 nM, respectively, whereas the most effective P1-targeted compound, AA 29504, was active at 10 μM.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: GNF 5837 displayed antiviral efficacy at 80 nM.
source: Two L1-selected compounds, KB SRC 4 and GNF 5837 displayed antiviral efficacy at 250 and 80 nM, respectively, whereas the most effective P1-targeted compound, AA 29504, was active at 10 μM.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: AA 29504 was active at 10 μM.
source: Two L1-selected compounds, KB SRC 4 and GNF 5837 displayed antiviral efficacy at 250 and 80 nM, respectively, whereas the most effective P1-targeted compound, AA 29504, was active at 10 μM.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: GNF 5837 displayed in vitro EC50 values at sub-micromolar concentrations.
source: These leading hit compounds were re-tested in a second round of plaque-reduction assays, confirming efficacy (Figure 6E) and displayed in vitro EC50 values at similar orders of magnitude as their observed potency in cell culture, namely sub-micromolar for GNF 5837, and approximately 10 µM for AA 29504 (Figure 6F, G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: AA 29504 displayed in vitro EC50 values at approximately 10 µM.
source: These leading hit compounds were re-tested in a second round of plaque-reduction assays, confirming efficacy (Figure 6E) and displayed in vitro EC50 values at similar orders of magnitude as their observed potency in cell culture, namely sub-micromolar for GNF 5837, and approximately 10 µM for AA 29504 (Figure 6F, G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Drug treatment specifically reduced infectivity within the high-density infectious fraction compared to controls.
source: Drug treatment specifically reduced infectivity (measured at 1:10 supernatant dilution to maintain both species) within the high-density infectious fraction compared to controls; the lower-density fractions were unaffected (Figure 7A, B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: Specific infectivity within the high-density fraction normalised by RT-qPCR for ZIKV RNA was significantly reduced following exposure to inhibitors.
source: Importantly, as well as a global loss of infectivity, specific infectivity within the high-density fraction normalised by (reverse transcriptase quantitative polymerase chain reaction) RT-qPCR for ZIKV RNA (E gene target) was also significantly reduced (Figure 7C), meaning that intact virions were rendered less infectious following exposure to inhibitors rather than being physically disrupted via non-specific 'virolysis'.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Intact virions were rendered less infectious following exposure to inhibitors rather than being physically disrupted via non-specific 'virolysis'.
source: Importantly, as well as a global loss of infectivity, specific infectivity within the high-density fraction normalised by (reverse transcriptase quantitative polymerase chain reaction) RT-qPCR for ZIKV RNA (E gene target) was also significantly reduced (Figure 7C), meaning that intact virions were rendered less infectious following exposure to inhibitors rather than being physically disrupted via non-specific 'virolysis'.
evidence: This is an inference based on the specific infectivity data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Rimantadine treatment prevented viraemia in a preclinical ZIKV infection model.
source: RT-qPCR analysis confirmed equivalent copies of viral RNA present within tissues at the inoculation site (Figure 8B), whereas viraemia was dramatically reduced within rimantadine-treated animals, measured by BHK cell plaque assay (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Rimantadine exerted an antiviral effect in vivo that prevented dissemination of the virus.
source: Thus, rimantadine exerted an antiviral effect in vivo that prevented dissemination of the virus, consistent with cell culture observations, and supporting the druggability of M in vivo.
evidence: This is an inference based on the in vivo data shown in Figure 8.

claim: The rearrangement and formation of trimeric E complexes during acid-induced fusion may provide an opportunity for M to adopt alternative conformations.
source: We hypothesise that the rearrangement and formation of trimeric E complexes during acid-induced fusion may provide an opportunity for M to also adopt alternative conformations.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the known structural changes of E protein during fusion.

claim: Asymmetric formation of relatively few channel complexes may lead to a loss of signal upon application of icosahedral symmetry in cryo-EM reconstructions.
source: It is possible that asymmetric formation of relatively few channel complexes leads to a loss of signal upon application of icosahedral symmetry, or due to the overwhelming inherent symmetry of the particle.
evidence: This is speculation about why M is not visible in cryo-EM structures of acidified virions.

claim: C-terminal M-derived peptides from DENV type 1 formed cation-selective channels in suspended bilayers.
source: C-terminal M-derived peptides from DENV type 1 were shown to form cation-selective channels in suspended bilayers (Premkumar et al., 2005), with sensitivity to amantadine (10 μM) and higher concentrations of hexamethylene amiloride (100 μM).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Premkumar et al., 2005.

claim: DENV M-derived peptides showed sensitivity to amantadine (10 μM) and higher concentrations of hexamethylene amiloride (100 μM).
source: C-terminal M-derived peptides from DENV type 1 were shown to form cation-selective channels in suspended bilayers (Premkumar et al., 2005), with sensitivity to amantadine (10 μM) and higher concentrations of hexamethylene amiloride (100 μM).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Premkumar et al., 2005.

claim: DENV replication in human peripheral blood leukocytes and Rhesus macaque kidney epithelial cells (LLC-MK2) was suppressed by amantadine and rimantadine.
source: Older studies showed that DENV replication in human peripheral blood leukocytes and Rhesus macaque kidney epithelial cells (LLC-MK2) was suppressed by amantadine and rimantadine, with maximal effect when drugs were administered concomitant with infection (Koff et al., 1980), reminiscent of findings herein.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Koff et al., 1980.

claim: Maximal suppression of DENV replication by amantadine and rimantadine occurred when drugs were administered concomitant with infection.
source: Older studies showed that DENV replication in human peripheral blood leukocytes and Rhesus macaque kidney epithelial cells (LLC-MK2) was suppressed by amantadine and rimantadine, with maximal effect when drugs were administered concomitant with infection (Koff et al., 1980), reminiscent of findings herein.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Koff et al., 1980.

claim: The EC50 for rimantadine against ZIKV was between 10 and 20 μM.
source: The EC50 for rimantadine was between 10 and 20 μM, which is comparable to drug potency versus susceptible HCV strains (Griffin et al., 2008).
evidence: This is based on the experimental data shown in Figure 3A and comparison to published data.

claim: The EC50 for rimantadine against ZIKV is comparable to drug potency versus susceptible HCV strains.
source: The EC50 for rimantadine was between 10 and 20 μM, which is comparable to drug potency versus susceptible HCV strains (Griffin et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Griffin et al., 2008.

claim: M2 and SARS-CoV-2 E are the only examples where targeting a viroporin has been shown to exert preclinical antiviral efficacy.
source: To date only M2, and more recently SARS-CoV-2 E, are the only examples where targeting a viroporin has been shown to exert preclinical antiviral efficacy.
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge in the field.

claim: M channels are physiologically relevant drug targets.
source: Thus, our findings strongly support that M channels are also physiologically relevant drug targets.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the in vivo efficacy data shown in Figure 8.

claim: Monomer simulations indicated that a single trans-membrane-spanning topology was unstable resulting in the C-terminus folding back towards the plane of the membrane surface.
source: Importantly, monomer simulations indicated that a single trans-membrane-spanning topology was unstable resulting in the C-terminus folding back towards the plane of the membrane surface.
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Dual-trans-membrane topology protomers comprise the more energetically favourable conformation for mature M.
source: Hence, we considered that dual-trans-membrane topology protomers comprise the more energetically favourable conformation for mature M, as seen for multiple structures of mature Flavivirus virions (Sirohi et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an inference based on the simulation data and comparison to cryo-EM structures.

claim: The compact channel structure retained a lumen with a radius of 5.23 Å at its narrowest point.
source: The compact channel structure retained a lumen with a radius of 5.23 Å at its narrowest point, lined by Thr57, Val61, Ile62, Val65, Met66, Leu68, and Leu69 (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The compact channel lumen is lined by Thr57, Val61, Ile62, Val65, Met66, Leu68, and Leu69.
source: The compact channel structure retained a lumen with a radius of 5.23 Å at its narrowest point, lined by Thr57, Val61, Ile62, Val65, Met66, Leu68, and Leu69 (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Compact M hexamer channels initially allowed the formation of a water column, but then closed at Leu64 and Leu68.
source: Upon 200 ns atomistic simulation within a model POPC bilayer, channels initially allowed the formation of a water column, but then closed at Leu64 and Leu68, despite the former not facing the lumen at the beginning of the simulation (Figure 5C–E).
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 5C-E.

claim: GNF 5837 is a potent inhibitor of TrKs A, B, and C.
source: GNF 5837 is a potent inhibitor of TrKs A, B, and C, high-affinity receptors for nerve growth factor that regulate neuronal survival and differentiation (Albaugh et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Albaugh et al., 2012.

claim: GNF 5837 has an IC50 of ~10 nM against its cognate targets (TrKs).
source: GNF 5837 has an IC50 of ~10 nM against its cognate targets, yet only achieved an antiviral ~EC50 at 80 nM in BHK cell plaque-reduction assays.
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge about GNF 5837.

claim: TrK expression is primarily restricted to the CNS and the thyroid, with only very low expression in kidney tissues.
source: Importantly, TrK expression is primarily restricted to the (central nervous system) CNS and the thyroid, with only very low expression in kidney tissues according to the human protein atlas.
evidence: This statement is based on data from the human protein atlas.

claim: KB SRC 4 has an in vitro Ki of 44 nM versus c-Src.
source: KB SRC 4 has an in vitro Ki of 44 nM versus c-Src (higher against other Src-related kinases), whilst GSK 2837808A has an IC50 of 2.6 and 43 nM against LDHA/B, respectively; the former impeded cell metabolic activity at 500 nM, whilst the latter had no effect.
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge about KB SRC 4.

claim: GSK 2837808A has an IC50 of 2.6 and 43 nM against LDHA/B, respectively.
source: KB SRC 4 has an in vitro Ki of 44 nM versus c-Src (higher against other Src-related kinases), whilst GSK 2837808A has an IC50 of 2.6 and 43 nM against LDHA/B, respectively; the former impeded cell metabolic activity at 500 nM, whilst the latter had no effect.
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge about GSK 2837808A.

claim: KB SRC 4 impeded cell metabolic activity at 500 nM.
source: KB SRC 4 has an in vitro Ki of 44 nM versus c-Src (higher against other Src-related kinases), whilst GSK 2837808A has an IC50 of 2.6 and 43 nM against LDHA/B, respectively; the former impeded cell metabolic activity at 500 nM, whilst the latter had no effect.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: GSK 2837808A had no effect on cell metabolic activity.
source: KB SRC 4 has an in vitro Ki of 44 nM versus c-Src (higher against other Src-related kinases), whilst GSK 2837808A has an IC50 of 2.6 and 43 nM against LDHA/B, respectively; the former impeded cell metabolic activity at 500 nM, whilst the latter had no effect.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: Formoterol is a long-acting β2-adrenergic receptor agonist (IC50 in pM range), used as a bronchodilator in the treatment of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
source: Formoterol is a long-acting β2-adrenergic receptor agonist (IC50 in pM range), used as a bronchodilator in the treatment of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (Berger and Nadel, 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Berger and Nadel, 2008.

claim: L-732 183 is a potent competitive tachykinin NK1 receptor antagonist (IC50 = 2.3 nM).
source: L-732 183 is a potent competitive tachykinin NK1 receptor antagonist (IC50 = 2.3 nM), the receptor for substance P (Quartara and Maggi, 1997), whilst AA 29504 (Vardya et al., 2012) is a positive allosteric modulator of GABAA receptors (IC50 = 9–13 μM).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Quartara and Maggi, 1997.

claim: AA 29504 is a positive allosteric modulator of GABAA receptors (IC50 = 9–13 μM).
source: L-732 183 is a potent competitive tachykinin NK1 receptor antagonist (IC50 = 2.3 nM), the receptor for substance P (Quartara and Maggi, 1997), whilst AA 29504 (Vardya et al., 2012) is a positive allosteric modulator of GABAA receptors (IC50 = 9–13 μM).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Vardya et al., 2012.

claim: GABAA receptors are not expressed in the kidney.
source: Notably, this is less clear in terms of differential potency of AA 29504, although, much like the case for GNF 5837, GABAA receptors, the target of AA 29504, are not expressed in the kidney.
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge.

claim: Compounds specifically reduced infectivity in the major high-density peak, but not in a lower-density region of the gradient.
source: Interestingly, compounds specifically reduced infectivity in the major high-density peak, but not in a lower-density region of the gradient where lower levels of infectivity were susceptible to relatively low serial dilutions; this was not the case for the high-density peak.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: The FDA classes rimantadine as a class C drug during pregnancy.
source: The FDA classes rimantadine as a class C drug during pregnancy, that is administered if the potential benefit might outweigh the risk.
evidence: This statement is presented as established regulatory information.

claim: Rimantadine will cross mouse placentas.
source: Whilst rimantadine will cross mouse placentas, eleven times the maximum recommended human dose (MRHD) is necessary to become embryotoxic.
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge about rimantadine.

claim: Eleven times the MRHD of rimantadine is necessary to become embryotoxic in mice.
source: Whilst rimantadine will cross mouse placentas, eleven times the maximum recommended human dose (MRHD) is necessary to become embryotoxic.
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge about rimantadine.

claim: 3.4 and 6.8 times the MRHD of rimantadine increased pup mortality up to 4 days post-partum in mice.
source: However, 3.4 and 6.8 times the MRHD did increase pup mortality up to 4 days post-partum, yet this still by far exceeds the dose used during influenza prophylaxis in the past (Product Information. Flumadine (rimantadine). Forest Pharmaceuticals, St. Louis, MO. 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to product information.

claim: No controlled studies of rimantadine have been undertaken during human pregnancy.
source: No controlled studies have been undertaken during human pregnancy, but faced with the alternative of microcephaly, the balance of risk may be favourable.
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge about rimantadine.

claim: The generic status of rimantadine means that it could be deployed rapidly at minimal cost to areas of endemic ZIKV infection or during outbreaks.
source: The generic status of rimantadine also means that it could be deployed rapidly at minimal cost to areas of endemic ZIKV infection or during outbreaks, which overwhelmingly tend to occur in lower/middle income countries (LMICs).
evidence: This is an inference based on the generic status of rimantadine.

claim: ZIKV outbreaks overwhelmingly tend to occur in lower/middle income countries (LMICs).
source: The generic status of rimantadine also means that it could be deployed rapidly at minimal cost to areas of endemic ZIKV infection or during outbreaks, which overwhelmingly tend to occur in lower/middle income countries (LMICs).
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge about ZIKV epidemiology.

claim: M peptides migrated as higher-order structures when reconstituted in DH6PC.
source: Consistent with the formation an aqueous pore across the membrane, ZIKV M peptides migrated as higher-order structures when reconstituted in the membrane-mimetic detergent, DH6PC.
evidence: This is supported by native PAGE data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: M peptides formed potential hexamers or heptamers based on native PAGE.
source: These corresponded to potential hexamers or heptamers, albeit estimated by native PAGE, and were confirmed to adopt a channel-like architecture using TEM.
evidence: This is supported by native PAGE data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: M complexes adopted a channel-like architecture confirmed by TEM.
source: These corresponded to potential hexamers or heptamers, albeit estimated by native PAGE, and were confirmed to adopt a channel-like architecture using TEM.
evidence: This is supported by TEM data shown in Figure 1B and C.

claim: M complexes mediated membrane bilayer permeability using an indirect ion channel assay, based upon fluorescent dye release from liposomes.
source: Nevertheless, M complexes mediated membrane bilayer permeability using an indirect ion channel assay, based upon fluorescent dye release from liposomes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Rimantadine sensitivity supports that dye release was mediated by interactions with a folded protein complex rather than via aggregates disrupting membrane integrity.
source: Importantly, rimantadine sensitivity supports that dye release was mediated by interactions with a folded protein complex rather than via aggregates disrupting membrane integrity, and increased activity at acidic pH is consistent with activation within acidifying endosomes during virus entry.
evidence: This is an inference based on the rimantadine sensitivity data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Increased M activity at acidic pH is consistent with activation within acidifying endosomes during virus entry.
source: Importantly, rimantadine sensitivity supports that dye release was mediated by interactions with a folded protein complex rather than via aggregates disrupting membrane integrity, and increased activity at acidic pH is consistent with activation within acidifying endosomes during virus entry.
evidence: This is an inference based on the pH sensitivity data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Rimantadine was most effective when added prior to and simultaneously with infectious innoculae.
source: Rimantadine was most effective when added prior to and simultaneously with infectious innoculae, suggesting that pre-loading of endocytic vesicles with the drug may expedite the inhibition of virion-resident channels.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Pre-loading of endocytic vesicles with rimantadine may expedite the inhibition of virion-resident channels.
source: Rimantadine was most effective when added prior to and simultaneously with infectious innoculae, suggesting that pre-loading of endocytic vesicles with the drug may expedite the inhibition of virion-resident channels.
evidence: This is speculation based on the timing of rimantadine effects.

claim: Rimantadine may exert a drug rescue effect upon cells during multi-cycle replication, lessening the cytopathic effects of ZIKV infection.
source: We are uncertain why this should be the case, yet we speculate that in addition to inhibitory properties, rimantadine may also exert a drug rescue effect upon cells during multi-cycle replication, lessening the cytopathic effects of ZIKV infection and thereby artificially inflating the number of surviving cells remaining at the end of the assay.
evidence: This is speculation to explain an observation about rimantadine effects.
